messages:
Maya (CS): looping everyone in — quick post-cutover check for Chromis private/VPC onboarding. main open items: audit log retention alignment, KMS key access across accounts, and a tiny IAM role gap discovered during smoke tests. want to get owners and dates.
Diego (Chromis PM): thanks — saw the smoke tests. audit logs were coming through but retention in their Splunk is set to 7d; we expected 90d. that's the blocker for my compliance team.
Arjun (Solutions): ok can you paste the Splunk index name and where retention is configured? also which log streams are currently forwarded (vpc_flow, app_logs, agent_metrics)?
Diego (Chromis PM): index=redwood-priv-chromis, forwarding: vpc_flow, app_logs. agent_metrics is currently disabled (we turned off during test).
Lena (Security Eng): retention mismatch is usually a retention policy on the SIEM side, but we also need to ensure our router isn't sampling-out older batches. two checks: 1) confirm delivery timestamps are complete for older files, 2) ensure the collector isn't deleting local buffers after 24h.
Maya (CS): Action: Arjun to confirm router buffer policy & forwarding config by EOD tomorrow. Lena to draft secure KMS cross-account policy and rotation note by Friday. Diego to get compliance acceptance once we confirm retention. I'll own tracking and follow-up.
Arjun (Solutions): quick note — router buffer config is in the envoy config on the priv-gw instance. snippet below:
```
# envoy snippet
transport_socket: tls
cluster: splunk-collector
buffer_limits: { max_entries: 5000, max_bytes: 104857600 }
# retention: local temp files purged after 24h by default-cleanup cron
```
Arjun (Solutions): I will update the cleanup cron to 7 days for the collector host (non-production path) and verify end-to-end delivery of 90d files to Splunk test index.
Lena (Security Eng): KMS: Chromis uses a customer-managed key in their account. we need an IAM Role in their account allowing our ingest role to decrypt envelopes for routing. Proposed policy (high level):
- grant kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey on key ARN to role arn:aws:iam::<redwood-account>:role/priv-ingest
- require key policy to include aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn constraints
Maya (CS): Diego — would Chromis be ok with a role ARN in their account that we assume for ingestion?
Diego (Chromis PM): yes that's fine, compliance prefers least-priv. they asked about key rotation frequency though — we currently rotate every 365 days.
Lena (Security Eng): 365d is acceptable. we'll add automated rotation with a scheduled KMS re-encrypt plan and document the rollover steps in the runbook. also add steps for emergency key rollback (manual with approval).
Arjun (Solutions): small IAM gap found during smoke: our ingestion role expects a tag 'environment=chromis' but their role hasn't propagated tags. two options: we add an explicit principal condition or they add tags. which do we prefer?
Diego (Chromis PM): easier for us to tag on our side, but tagging in infra-as-code is quick. i'll add the tag today.
Maya (CS): updated action list: 1) Arjun — change collector cleanup cron to 7d and validate delivery to index redwood-priv-chromis (due: +1 business day). 2) Arjun + Lena — provide exact KMS key policy snippet for Chromis to apply (due: Fri COB). 3) Diego — apply role tag environment=chromis and confirm (due: today). 4) Lena — add rotation/rollback steps to priv-deploy runbook and share (due: Fri). I'll ping again in 48h. :spiral_calendar: 
infra-bot: Deploy monitor: priv-gw-collector updated (config change queued) — run id: d-4821.
Arjun (Solutions): confirmed queued change. i'll run smoke after deploy and post results.
Diego (Chromis PM): thanks team. one more ask from compliance — they want a short one-paragraph statement we can attach to their audit saying logs are retained for 90d, KMS keys are customer-managed with rotation policy, and access is least-priv. can someone draft?
Lena (Security Eng): I'll draft that and keep it factual. short version: "Chromis ingestion is configured to forward VPC flow and application logs to the Chromis-managed Splunk index 'redwood-priv-chromis' with retention configured to 90 days. Cryptographic material is protected by a customer-managed AWS KMS key in Chromis account; Redwood assumes a dedicated cross-account role with least-privilege for decryption during ingestion. Key rotation is scheduled every 365 days and emergency rollback procedures are documented in the private deploy runbook."
Maya (CS): perfect. Diego — i'll attach Lena's paragraph to the customer audit packet and mark the account health as 'amber' until EOD Friday (pending runbook + validation).
Diego (Chromis PM): amber is fine. will confirm once tagging is done. thanks all. :thumbsup:
Maya (CS): closing note — follow-up call scheduled Thu 10am; i'll send calendar invite. if anything blocks earlier, ping me in this thread.
